content.thinking:
I should check the val directory for the validator and plan out the layout: since the workspace's in/ dir on node-2 is read-only, I'll add a new in/partkit/ subfolder for the partkit files and specs, keeping a local copy under agent-notes, and run the sandbox via blender invoking the harness script with the spec file and name.

I'll name the new harness and template files with a pk_ prefix so they stay separate from the first PoC's files, and use pk- prefixes for shared sandbox output too. For the design itself, I'm setting coordinates with +X as muzzle direction, Z up, and receiver centreline at y=0 in meters, then deciding to write self-contained geometry helpers in a pk_geo.py module using bmesh directly (bevel box, tapered prism, cylinder along X) rather than relying on bpy.ops, since that should be faster and keep the kit independent of the original harness.

Each part will be a function returning named geometry tagged by material slot — metal, furniture, barrel, mag, accent — with parts grouped into functional objects like receiver, handguard, magazine, stock, grip, barrel, sights, and accent, each getting its own material and UV unwrap via smart projection so everything stays UV-ready and properly named.

Now I'm sketching out the spec schema itself: fields for receiver style/length/height/width, barrel length/profile/radius/muzzle type, gas tube flag, handguard style and length, magazine style/capacity/curve/position, stock style and length, grip style, and sights front/rear options — essentially a parameter dictionary that drives the whole generative template.

I'm also planning the required variant count: at least three to four options per major part type. For receivers I'm thinking ak_stamped, modern_slab, smg_boxy, and bullpup_shell; for handguards wood_ak, rail_quad, slim_poly, and a perforated shroud style; for magazines curved banana, straight box, and drum; and for stocks fixed_wood, fixed_poly, folding_wire, folding_side, and a bullpup-integral option.

I'm also sketching how glow accent strips would work as emissive material along the receiver/handguard edges, and now I'm working out how to handle bullpup versus conventional layouts -- defining anchor points for the receiver body, grip, magazine well, barrel, handguard, and stock position so each receiver style can compute its own geometry offsets.

Then I'm designing the core geometry helper library for building parts out of bmesh primitives -- boxes, cylinders, and extruded profiles -- with bevel support that selectively rounds edges based on their angle rather than beveling everything uniformly.

Writing the merge helper function...

For primitive shapes, I'll use bmesh.ops.create_cone for cylinders (rotated from Z to X axis), create_cube scaled for boxes, and build custom vert/face data for prisms.

Concave profile polygons should be fine since the glTF exporter handles triangulation itself. I'm planning to apply bevels selectively, only on edges exceeding a certain angle threshold, using bmesh.ops.bevel with adjustable offset and segment count.

I'm staying mindful of the triangle budget—keeping bevel segments to 1 (a simple chamfer) to minimize triangle count, which should keep the total well under 10,000. For shading, I'm leaning toward flat shading for hard-surface parts but smooth shading for cylindrical faces, though I need to watch out for how caps are handled separately from the curved sides.

Instead of relying on bevels for cylinder caps, I'll mark sharp edges using bmesh's edge-smooth flag for angles exceeding 40 degrees, while setting faces to smooth—trusting that the glTF exporter respects these sharp-edge markings when computing split normals, rather than defaulting everything to flat as the earlier version did.

For UVs, smart_project at the end per object is simpler and better for baking than a manual per-face dominant-axis projection, so I'll stick with it. I also need to let each primitive declare its own material slot, since a part like a handguard can mix metal and wood primitives, with the bmesh tracking per-face material indices accordingly.

I'll just set each face's material_index to its global slot index while building, then at object creation assign the full ordered slot list as materials — unused slots are harmless since glTF export only emits primitives for materials actually used. That keeps things simple, so now I'm turning to naming the actual part objects: receiver, handguard, magazine, stock, grip, barrel, sights, trim.

For materials I'm sticking with default palette slots (body, furniture, barrel, mag, accent, glow) defined by hex colors with optional metal flags, plus an emissive glow slot, and I'm setting up x-forward/z-up/y-side coordinates before defining receiver geometry variants like the stamped AK receiver with its dust cover, trunnion, and safety lever placement.

Working out anchor positions...

Bore axis sits at z=0 for both conventional and bullpup layouts, with the receiver centered vertically around it and the stock extending rearward. For receiver styles, I'm defining the stamped AK look with its half-cylinder dust cover on top, and starting on the modern slab-sided upper receiver geometry.

For the SMG prompt, I'll model the magazine as emerging directly from the bottom of the grip rather than from a separate well, so the grip draws first and the magazine box starts just below it, with a small overlapping stub to make the insertion look seamless.

I'm making the magazine narrower than the grip so it stays visually tucked inside, letting only the lower portion stick out below the grip for that UZI-style look. Next I'm starting on the bullpup receiver shape, defining its long profile as a polygon extending back from the stock.

I also want a top rail integrated over the shell for sights or an optic. For the bullpup layout, I'm setting receiver length to about 0.55, with the stock attaching at x0 and grip/mag/barrel/trigger positions calculated as offsets from there, and the handguard beginning just forward of the grip.

Writing handguard variants...

Also sketching a perforated barrel shroud with ribbed cylinder segments for a sci-fi look. For magazines, I'm planning distinct shapes anchored at the mag position: a curved banana mag with capacity-based length scaling, a straight box mag with slight taper and forward cant, and a drum mag using a cylinder along the y-axis.

For stocks, I'm defining three types attached at the stock position relative to the bore line: a fixed wood stock as a simple tapered prism, a fixed polymer stock with a tapered profile and a cheek rest plus rubber pad detail, and I'm starting on a folding wire stock as well.

For the folding wire stock, I'm building it from two rods running back from the receiver connected by a U-shaped buttplate, with a boolean parameter controlling whether it's shown extended or folded against the receiver side — I'll default to extended since that's more visually recognizable for an SMG. I'm also planning a folding side stock variant similar in construction, just differing in how the skeleton tubes fold.

Now mapping out the remaining stock variants: folding_side as a hinged flat bar frame arm with shoulder plate (CZ Scorpion style), bullpup_integral with buttpad and cheek riser, and a plain cap plate for "none" — five stock types total. For grips, I'm settling on ak_slanted, raked_poly, and vertical plus none, with trigger and trigger guard grouped into a combined "grip" part. For the barrel, I'm listing profile options: plain cylinder, tapered cone, heavy (larger radius), and fluted.

Muzzle devices include the AK slant brake (cylinder with ring), flash hider (slotted cylinder with thin prongs), suppressor (larger cylinder), and none/crown. I'm adding a gas tube as a boolean — a cylinder running above the barrel from gas block to handguard top, with the gas block always present when the tube exists. Barrel length is measured as the exposed length from receiver front to muzzle, including the portion inside the handguard.

For sights, front options are post (block plus post), hooded (ring plus post), or none, positioned near the muzzle just before any muzzle device; rear options are tangent (AK ramp), notch (flip sight), carry_handle (bridge), red_dot (box with lens glow), or none, anchored to the receiver's sight position. I'm also defining an accent/glow strip system — a list of colored emissive strips that can be placed on the receiver, handguard, stock, magazine, or barrel, either on the side or top, with configurable color and emission strength.

For implementation, each glow strip is a thin box slot running along the target part's extents — along the receiver or handguard length at the midline, or as a magazine window — from a fixed set of known placements (receiver_side, handguard_side, receiver_top, magazine_window, barrel_ring, stock_side), with colors drawn from the glow palette. Overall scale varies by weapon type, with rifles around 0.85-1.0 length and SMGs around 0.5-0.6.

Now I'm turning to the harness script — it needs to load the spec JSON, import the build template, and handle mesh joining, UV mapping, stats, GLB export, and rendering, reusing the render/stats logic from the previous harness since that's fixed infrastructure rather than model-generated content. I'm planning three render views (side, three-quarter, top-ish) matching the previous angle conventions, aiming for a final three-view sheet per prompt.

For the camera setup, azimuth 0 should look along the correct axis so the muzzle appears on the right side of the frame, which checks out. I'll keep the lighting and Cycles render settings similar to before, maybe trimming sample count slightly to save time across three renders per round, and I want to check what's already in the validator directory before deciding what extra checks (manifold edges, UV, shell counts) are worth adding versus skipping as unnecessary. For token accounting, I need to estimate costs from the JSON output tokens plus schema context plus image token costs for each render.

I'm figuring the contact sheet image read cost will be smaller than naive math suggests since the Read tool downsamples large images, so reading one combined sheet per round instead of separate images should keep costs down. I'm also thinking I could use a compact cached schema card to reduce the per-prompt overhead, and I'm wondering whether I can just track actual usage via the token counter shown in system reminders, though it's unclear if that reflects true per-call cost or the whole context size.

The decrease between successive counter readings (14955045 → 14949368, about 5.7k) seems to match incremental tool-result text rather than total context, suggesting it's a delta I can use to measure actual cost per prompt step, as long as I keep my own reasoning tight during the AI step. Now I want to check the val directory before moving on to writing the code files -- starting with geometry helpers, then variant parts, rifle templates, and the harness script, making sure sibling imports resolve properly via sys.path insertion.

Since the harness computes its directory from the script location and the input folder is read-only, Python's bytecode caching will fail quietly, so I should disable it with sys.dont_write_bytecode. I'm planning to keep source files locally and sync them to the node's input folder, writing my own run script for that.

Setting up the Part class with bmesh, defining slot ordering and material index assignment...

Writing bevel helper, clamping width relative to geometry size, and adding a transform helper for placing parts using translation and Euler rotation matrices. Now sketching box and cylinder primitive methods that scale a base mesh, bevel edges, then place them in world space.

Working out cylinder axis rotations so cones align along x, y, or z while keeping bevel limited to cap edges, then starting a generic prism helper for profile-based extrusions along different planes.

For the cap faces, I'll just let Blender's recalc_face_normals and ngon triangulation handle concave shapes correctly. Now I'm defining the final conversion method that turns a part's mesh data into an actual Blender object with materials assigned.

I'm marking edges sharp based on face angle so bevels stay crisp while flat regions stay smooth, then building the mesh and object from the bmesh data. I'm slightly worried about normal blending artifacts on the tiny 0.003 chamfer with only one segment, since that creates very thin faces whose edges might get mismarked by the angle threshold.

Now I'm setting up material generation—iterating through palette entries to build Principled BSDF materials per slot with color, metal, roughness, and emission defaults, keeping in mind that emission strength above 1 needs KHR_materials_emissive_strength for glTF export.

I'm moving on to writing the part-generation functions, each taking parts/spec/anchors dictionaries, starting with the AK receiver geometry using length, height, and width parameters to build the base box. Defining receiver box dimensions...

Still working out the handguard positioning relative to the receiver front...

Still defining receiver boxes...

Still placing gun part geometry...

Applying the same ordering to the AR grip, trigger, and magazine positions, then moving to defining the SMG receiver dimensions with its length, height, width, and bevel parameters.

Working out the SMG features next—the ribbed top cover, charging knob, ejection port, and front cap ring as a cylinder—plus placing the magazine relative to the grip and figuring out the trigger offset, since for an UZI-style layout the grip sits below the receiver and the trigger needs to sit forward of it.

Checking against the AK reference measurements to calibrate that offset: there the trigger sits about 0.106 forward of the grip center, with the trigger guard enclosing the trigger area between roughly -0.17 and -0.064, and the grip front landing just behind the guard's rear edge. I'm using that relationship to estimate a shorter guard length for the SMG's proportionally more compact layout.

Still shaping bullpup body profile...

Still defining the body profile...

Working out the bullpup layout logic: grip placement sits mid-body with the trigger guard forward of it and the magazine behind, matching the FAMAS/AUG/Tavor convention, which stays consistent with the AK-style anchoring I set up.

Sketching the build function that assembles parts by name and calls the appropriate receiver-style constructor, with glowing trim strips layered on top. I'm settling on an assembly order: receiver, grip, magazine, stock, barrel plus gas system, handguard, sights, then accents.

Now I'm working out the barrel geometry -- positioning it along the x-axis from the receiver's edge, calculating its center point, and handling different profiles (plain, tapered, heavy). I'm also figuring out muzzle device variants like brakes, flash hiders, and suppressors with their own dimensions, plus placing the gas block at an offset near the barrel's end.

I'm now computing the gas tube position relative to the barrel axis, deciding how far forward it extends toward the gas block, and noting that the handguard will hide most of it -- only the portion beyond the handguard stays visible.

Setting default handguard length to 0.26, then laying out the wood AK upper handguard as a cylinder positioned slightly above bore with its own radius and length.

I'm working out the lower handguard box dimensions and bevel, plus groove count, then reconciling the receiver centerline offset relative to bore so the cover and box heights line up correctly for the AK coordinate system.

Shifting the remaining grip, trigger guard, and magazine coordinates down by 0.012 to match the new reference frame, keeping the magazine radius and rotation consistent with the original model.

I'll apply a slight forward cant by rotating the magazine box around the top point, computing the bottom center using a direction vector based on the cant angle so the bottom shifts forward, similar to the slight forward curve seen on AK-style magazines.

For the rounded drum magazine, I'm computing a cylinder with ribbed rims and a connecting neck box, while for stocks I'm beginning with a fixed wooden stock shape attached at the stock position.

Converting the absolute stock points into coordinates relative to the receiver, then parameterizing them as fractions of a length variable so the stock profile can scale with different lengths.

Still working out the stock polygon coordinates...

Now I'm adding the folding wire assembly: two parallel rods running along the stock with a butt-plate box at the rear and a sloped brace rod connecting them.

Using a quaternion rotation from the Z-axis to the target direction gives a robust general method, so I'll apply that for all diagonal rods, the gas tube, and wire stock. For the folded stock variant, I'll keep it simple: rods run forward along the sides of the receiver outside its width, with a vertical buttplate at the front end — noting this configuration is less certain and may need verification.

For the side-folding type, I'm thinking through a single-strut design like a CZ/Scorpion stock, with a hinge block at the rear and a flat bar frame running along one side connecting to a shoulder plate.

For the bullpup integral stock, I'm defining a buttpad with a slot cutout and a cheek riser prism sitting on top, plus the end cap for the "none" option. Then moving on to grip definitions, starting with the AK slanted grip as an angled box positioned relative to the receiver and trigger location.

Working through the grip geometry, I'm setting the vertical center so the grip bottom overlaps slightly into the receiver, and establishing a generic formula tying grip center height to the receiver's grip_z offset. I'm also reasoning through the Y-axis rotation direction confirming a positive angle rakes the top forward and kicks the bottom backward for a natural grip angle, with length and rake as the key parameters before moving to the raked grip variant.

Now I'm defining the grip's cross-section profile as a set of relative points tracing the backstrap curve and finger grooves, then applying a shear transform so x shifts proportionally with z to realize the rake angle across the whole shape.

Working out the trigger guard's ring geometry next, offsetting a set of x/z coordinates relative to the trigger position to form the loop shape...

Confirming the guard offset checks out, then I'm setting up the trigger box geometry with its rotation, and moving on to defining front sight positioning relative to the muzzle base.

Working out the front sight block and post dimensions...

For hooded sights I'll use side ear boxes flanking the post instead of a disc ring. For rear sights, I'm planning tangent and notch styles as simple box pairs, plus a carry handle made from two posts and a bridging bar with an aperture.

Still working out optic details...

For a curved mag, I'll approximate by placing a small box at the arc's midpoint rotated to match the tangent. I'm also sketching stock-side strips, barrel rings near the muzzle, and deciding to skip rail-top accents, then moving on to defining the color palette structure with hex keys for body, furniture, barrel, mag, accent, glow, and dark, plus default metalness values per part.

I'm now planning how the spec controls sizing (default scale, named length fields like receiver.length, hardcoded bevel widths) and UV unwrapping via smart_project after parenting objects. Writing bmesh construction code...

For rod placement I'll build the cone geometry then transform its vertices using the computed translation and rotation matrix after beveling. Time to start writing the general code.

Writing mesh generation helper...

I need to be careful about degenerate geometry when points are duplicated or collinear, since face creation could fail. Now moving to the template modules, defining helper defaults like `g(S, key, default)` and setting up the material palette for body, furniture, and barrel colors with their metal and roughness values.

Continuing the palette: magazine, accent, glow (cyan emission default), and dark slots with their respective colors and roughness, plus converting hex to linear RGB with a gamma approximation. For object naming, I'm mapping parts like receiver, grip, magazine, stock, handguard, barrel, sights, and trim to their appropriate material slots -- receiver uses body, small details and sights use dark/barrel steel, trim gets the glow slot.

Writing the material setup script...

I'll skip extra tapering details for now and focus on the magazine's curved prism, making sure its bevel edges stay above the 35° threshold. I'm also considering optional sci-fi touches like a muzzle block on the bullpup receiver, but I should just start writing the code carefully and fix errors as they come up.

# pk_parts.py -- PARTS KIT: reusable variants. Each fn(P, S, A): P=dict of Parts, S=its spec section, A=shared anchor dict.
# Frame: +X muzzle, Z up, bore axis z=0, y=0 centreline, metres. Receiver rear face at x=0.
import math
from mathutils import Vector

def g(S, k, d): return S.get(k, d) if S else d
def shear(pts, k): return [(x + z * k, z) for x, z in pts]

# ---------------- RECEIVERS (set anchors) ----------------
def recv_ak(P, S, A):
    R = P['receiver']; L = g(S, 'length', 0.36); h = g(S, 'height', 0.07); w = g(S, 'width', 0.046); zc = -0.017
    R.box((L / 2, 0, zc), (L, w, h), 'body', 0.004)
    R.cyl((L / 2, 0, 0.014), w / 2 + 0.0005, L - 0.01, 'body', seg=20)
    R.box((L + 0.012, 0, 0.0), (0.04, w - 0.004, 0.06), 'body', 0.005)
    R.box((L * 0.5, w / 2 + 0.002, -0.012), (L * 0.5, 0.004, 0.022), 'dark', 0.002)
    R.cyl((L * 0.62, w / 2 + 0.007, 0.018), 0.006, 0.04, 'dark', axis='y', seg=10)
    R.cyl((L * 0.62, w / 2 + 0.029, 0.018), 0.011, 0.014, 'dark', axis='y', seg=12)
    A.update(x0=0, x1=L + 0.032, z_top=0.0385, zb=zc - h / 2, w=w, zmid=zc, grip_x=0.062, trig_x=0.168, mag_x=L - 0.09,
             mag_z=zc - h / 2 + 0.005, sight_x=L - 0.08, hg_x0=L - 0.005)

def _rail(R, x0, L, z, slot='barrel', wd=0.02):
    R.box((x0 + L / 2, 0, z), (L, wd, 0.008), slot)
    for i in range(int(L / 0.022)):
        R.box((x0 + 0.011 + i * 0.022, 0, z + 0.006), (0.011, wd, 0.005), slot)

def recv_modern(P, S, A):
    R = P['receiver']; L = g(S, 'length', 0.30); w = 0.042
    R.box((L / 2, 0, 0.022), (L, w - 0.004, 0.048), 'body', 0.003)
    R.box((L * 0.45, 0, -0.032), (L * 0.9, w, 0.062), 'body', 0.003)
    R.box((L * 0.68, 0, -0.082), (L * 0.30, w - 0.004, 0.04), 'body', 0.003)
    R.box((L * 0.5, w / 2 - 0.002 + 0.0006, 0.02), (L * 0.26, 0.002, 0.02), 'dark')
    R.box((-0.012, 0, 0.04), (0.03, 0.026, 0.012), 'dark', 0.002)
    R.cyl((L + 0.005, 0, 0), 0.022, 0.02, 'body', seg=16)
    _rail(R, 0.0, L, 0.050)
    A.update(x0=0, x1=L + 0.015, z_top=0.0595, zb=-0.063, w=w, zmid=0.0, grip_x=0.055, trig_x=0.145, mag_x=L * 0.68,
             mag_z=-0.062, sight_x=L * 0.5, hg_x0=L - 0.01)

def recv_smg(P, S, A):
    R = P['receiver']; L = g(S, 'length', 0.27); w = g(S, 'width', 0.05); h = 0.062
    R.box((L / 2, 0, -0.002), (L, w, h), 'body', 0.007)
    R.box((L / 2, 0, h / 2 - 0.002 + 0.0008), (L * 0.9, 0.018, 0.004), 'dark')
    R.box((-0.006, 0, -0.002), (0.02, w - 0.006, h - 0.008), 'body', 0.004)
    R.cyl((L + 0.008, 0, 0), 0.028, 0.02, 'body', seg=16)
    R.box((L * 0.4, w / 2 + 0.0006, 0.004), (L * 0.22, 0.002, 0.018), 'dark')
    R.cyl((L * 0.55, w / 2 + 0.008, 0.012), 0.005, 0.016, 'dark', axis='y', seg=8)
    R.cyl((L * 0.55, w / 2 + 0.02, 0.012), 0.009, 0.01, 'dark', axis='y', seg=10)
    gx = L * 0.55
    A.update(x0=0, x1=L + 0.018, z_top=h / 2 - 0.002, zb=-0.002 - h / 2, w=w, zmid=-0.002, grip_x=gx, trig_x=gx + 0.075,
             mag_x=gx, mag_z=-0.002 - h / 2, sight_x=L * 0.15, hg_x0=L - 0.01, mag_in_grip=True)

def recv_bullpup(P, S, A):
    R = P['receiver']; L = g(S, 'length', 0.52); w = g(S, 'width', 0.05)
    pts = [(0, 0.04), (0.04, 0.06), (L * 0.55, 0.06), (L, 0.054), (L, -0.05), (L * 0.6, -0.06), (L * 0.33, -0.072), (0.03, -0.085), (0, -0.075)]
    R.prism(pts, w, 'body', 0.005)
    R.box((L * 0.34, w / 2 + 0.0006, 0.0), (L * 0.14, 0.002, 0.04), 'dark')
    if g(S, 'rail', True): _rail(R, L * 0.2, L * 0.7, 0.062)
    gx = L * 0.52
    A.update(x0=0, x1=L, z_top=0.0725 if g(S, 'rail', True) else 0.06, zb=-0.07, w=w, zmid=-0.01, grip_x=gx, trig_x=gx + 0.075,
             mag_x=gx - 0.115, mag_z=-0.07, sight_x=L * 0.42, hg_x0=L - 0.02, bullpup=True)
RECV = {'ak_stamped': recv_ak, 'modern_slab': recv_modern, 'smg_boxy': recv_smg, 'bullpup_shell': recv_bullpup}

# ---------------- GRIPS ----------------
def grip_ak(P, S, A):
    ln = g(S, 'length', 0.14); rk = g(S, 'rake', 0.38); zb = A['zb']
    P['grip'].box((A['grip_x'], 0, zb - ln / 2 + 0.018), (0.048, 0.046, ln), 'furniture', 0.009, rot=(0, rk, 0))
    A['grip_rake'] = rk
def grip_poly(P, S, A):
    ln = g(S, 'length', 0.13); rk = g(S, 'rake', 0.30); s = ln / 0.13; wd = g(S, 'width', 0.042)
    pts = [(-0.022, 0.01), (0.026, 0.01), (0.027, -0.03 * s), (0.022, -0.055 * s), (0.03, -0.085 * s), (0.022, -ln), (-0.03, -ln), (-0.026, -0.09 * s), (-0.032, -0.05 * s), (-0.024, -0.02 * s)]
    pts = [(x + A['grip_x'], z + A['zb'] + 0.01) for x, z in shear(pts, math.tan(rk))]
    P['grip'].prism(pts, wd, 'furniture', 0.004); A['grip_rake'] = rk
def grip_vertical(P, S, A):
    ln = g(S, 'length', 0.11)
    P['grip'].box((A['grip_x'], 0, A['zb'] - ln / 2 + 0.01), (0.044, 0.04, ln), 'furniture', 0.006)
    P['grip'].box((A['grip_x'], 0, A['zb'] - ln + 0.012), (0.05, 0.046, 0.012), 'dark', 0.003); A['grip_rake'] = 0.0
def grip_none(P, S, A): A['grip_rake'] = 0.0
GRIP = {'ak_slanted': grip_ak, 'raked_poly': grip_poly, 'vertical': grip_vertical, 'none': grip_none}

def trigger_guard(P, S, A):
    G = P['grip']; tx = A['trig_x']; zb = A['zb']; s = g(S, 'guard_scale', 1.0)
    dx = [-0.058, -0.056, -0.038, 0.027, 0.046, 0.048, 0.04, 0.038, 0.024, -0.036, -0.048, -0.05]
    dz = [0.006, -0.042, -0.053, -0.053, -0.035, 0.006, 0.006, -0.033, -0.045, -0.045, -0.037, 0.006]
    G.prism([(tx + x * s, zb + z * s) for x, z in zip(dx, dz)], 0.012, 'barrel', 0.0015)
    G.box((tx, 0, zb - 0.022), (0.006, 0.006, 0.034), 'barrel', 0.0015, rot=(0, -0.3, 0))

# ---------------- MAGAZINES ----------------
def mag_curved(P, S, A):
    cap = g(S, 'capacity', 30); arc = g(S, 'arc_length', 0.10 + cap * 0.0036); deg = g(S, 'curve_deg', 46); w = g(S, 'width', 0.04)
    R = arc / math.radians(deg); x0, z0 = A['mag_x'], A['mag_z']; N = 10; back, front = [], []
    for i in range(N + 1):
        ph = math.radians(deg) * i / N; cx, cz = x0 + R * (1 - math.cos(ph)), z0 - R * math.sin(ph)
        nx, nz = math.cos(ph), math.sin(ph); h = 0.026 + 0.008 * i / N
        back.append((cx - nx * h, cz - nz * h)); front.append((cx + nx * h, cz + nz * h))
    P['magazine'].prism(back + front[::-1], w, 'mag', 0.004)
    ph = math.radians(deg) * 0.5; A['mag_mid'] = (x0 + R * (1 - math.cos(ph)), z0 - R * math.sin(ph), -ph, w)
def mag_box(P, S, A):
    cap = g(S, 'capacity', 30); ln = g(S, 'length', 0.06 + cap * 0.0055); hd = g(S, 'depth', 0.024); w = g(S, 'width', 0.038)
    c = math.radians(g(S, 'cant_deg', 8))
    if A.get('mag_in_grip'): c = -A.get('grip_rake', 0.0); hd = min(hd, 0.02); w = min(w, 0.036)
    T = Vector((A['mag_x'], A['mag_z'])); d = Vector((math.sin(c), -math.cos(c))); n = Vector((math.cos(c), math.sin(c))); B = T + d * ln
    pts = [tuple(T - n * hd), tuple(T + n * hd), tuple(B + n * hd), tuple(B - n * hd)]
    P['magazine'].prism(pts, w, 'mag', 0.003)
    P['magazine'].box((B.x, 0, B.y + 0.004), (hd * 2 + 0.006, w + 0.004, 0.014), 'mag', 0.002, rot=(0, -c, 0))
    M = (T + B) / 2; A['mag_mid'] = (M.x, M.y, -c, w); A['mag_len'] = ln
def mag_drum(P, S, A):
    cap = g(S, 'capacity', 50); R = g(S, 'radius', 0.05 + cap * 0.0006); w = g(S, 'width', 0.055); cx, cz = A['mag_x'] + 0.012, A['mag_z'] - R - 0.022
    M = P['magazine']
    M.box((A['mag_x'], 0, A['mag_z'] - 0.012), (0.04, 0.04, 0.03), 'mag', 0.003)
    M.cyl((cx, 0, cz), R, w, 'mag', axis='y', seg=24, bevel=0.004)
    for sgn in (-1, 1): M.cyl((cx, sgn * (w / 2 - 0.002), cz), R * 0.8, 0.006, 'accent', axis='y', seg=20)
    M.cyl((cx, 0, cz), 0.018, w + 0.012, 'accent', axis='y', seg=12)
    A['mag_mid'] = (cx, cz, 0.0, w); A['mag_drum'] = True
MAG = {'curved': mag_curved, 'straight_box': mag_box, 'drum': mag_drum}

# ---------------- STOCKS ----------------
def stock_wood(P, S, A):
    Ls = g(S, 'length', 0.22); w = g(S, 'width', 0.04); St = P['stock']
    St.prism([(0.01, 0.03), (0.01 - Ls, 0.012), (0.005 - Ls, -0.112), (0.01 - 0.59 * Ls, -0.09), (0.01, -0.064)], w, 'furniture', 0.006)
    St.box((0.008 - Ls, 0, -0.05), (0.012, 0.042, 0.134), 'barrel', 0.003, rot=(0, -0.05, 0)); A['stock_len'] = Ls
def stock_poly(P, S, A):
    L = g(S, 'length', 0.24); w = g(S, 'width', 0.044); St = P['stock']
    St.cyl((-L * 0.25, 0, -0.004), 0.019, L * 0.6, 'body', seg=12)
    St.prism([(-L * 0.4, 0.04), (-L * 0.4, 0.05), (-L, 0.058), (-L, -0.09), (-L + 0.02, -0.095), (-L * 0.62, -0.04), (-L * 0.4, -0.03)], w, 'furniture', 0.004)
    St.box((-L - 0.004, 0, -0.016), (0.012, w + 0.004, 0.158), 'dark', 0.004); A['stock_len'] = L
def stock_wire(P, S, A):
    L = g(S, 'length', 0.24); St = P['stock']; wy = A['w'] / 2 + 0.008; zm = A['zmid'] + 0.012; folded = g(S, 'folded', False)
    sg = 1 if folded else -1; r = 0.0042; zb = zm - 0.075; xe = sg * L
    for s in (-1, 1):
        St.rod((0, s * wy, zm), (xe, s * wy, zm), r, 'barrel'); St.rod((xe * 0.35, s * wy, zm), (xe, s * wy, zb + 0.01), r, 'barrel')
        St.cyl((0.0, s * wy, zm), 0.009, 0.014, 'barrel', seg=10)
    St.rod((xe, -wy, zb + 0.01), (xe, wy, zb + 0.01), r, 'barrel')
    St.box((xe + sg * 0.004, 0, zm - 0.036), (0.012, wy * 2 + 0.01, 0.094), 'dark', 0.003); A['stock_len'] = L
def stock_strut(P, S, A):
    L = g(S, 'length', 0.22); St = P['stock']; wy = A['w'] / 2 + 0.01; zm = A['zmid']; folded = g(S, 'folded', False)
    sg = 1 if folded else -1; xe = sg * L
    for s in (-1, 1):
        St.box((xe / 2, s * wy, zm + 0.008), (L, 0.01, 0.02), 'body', 0.003)
        St.cyl((0, s * wy, zm + 0.008), 0.014, 0.016, 'barrel', axis='y', seg=14)
    St.prism([(xe, zm + 0.04), (xe + sg * 0.012, zm + 0.04), (xe + sg * 0.02, zm - 0.07), (xe, zm - 0.075)], 2 * wy, 'dark', 0.003)
    A['stock_len'] = L
def stock_bullpup(P, S, A):
    St = P['stock']; zm = A['zmid']
    St.box((-0.012, 0, zm - 0.02), (0.026, A['w'] + 0.006, 0.14), 'dark', 0.006)
    St.prism([(0.02, 0.06), (0.16, 0.06), (0.2, 0.074), (0.02, 0.074)], A['w'] - 0.008, 'furniture', 0.004); A['stock_len'] = 0.0
def stock_none(P, S, A):
    P['stock'].cyl((-0.006, 0, 0), 0.02, 0.012, 'body', seg=12); A['stock_len'] = 0.0
STOCK = {'fixed_wood': stock_wood, 'fixed_poly': stock_poly, 'folding_wire': stock_wire, 'folding_strut': stock_strut, 'bullpup_integral': stock_bullpup, 'none': stock_none}

# ---------------- HANDGUARDS ----------------
def hg_wood(P, S, A):
    H = P['handguard']; x = A['hg_x0']; Lh = g(S, 'length', 0.27)
    H.cyl((x + Lh * 0.315, 0, 0.028), 0.0215, Lh * 0.63, 'furniture', seg=18)
    H.box((x + Lh / 2, 0, -0.014), (Lh, 0.046, 0.052), 'furniture', 0.008)
    for k in range(4): H.box((x + 0.045 + k * 0.045 * Lh / 0.27, 0, -0.042), (0.012, 0.05, 0.006), 'barrel', 0.0015)
    A.update(hg_x1=x + Lh, hg_w=0.025, hg_zmid=-0.014, hg_covers_gas=True)
def hg_quad(P, S, A):
    H = P['handguard']; x = A['hg_x0']; Lh = g(S, 'length', 0.26); r = 0.0255
    H.cyl((x + Lh / 2, 0, 0), r, Lh, 'body', seg=16)
    for ang in range(4):
        a = ang * math.pi / 2; cy, cz = math.sin(a) * (r + 0.003), math.cos(a) * (r + 0.003)
        wy, wz = (0.018, 0.006) if ang % 2 == 0 else (0.006, 0.018)
        H.box((x + Lh / 2, cy, cz), (Lh, wy, wz), 'barrel')
        for i in range(int(Lh / 0.022)):
            H.box((x + 0.011 + i * 0.022, cy * 1.0 + math.sin(a) * 0.004, cz + math.cos(a) * 0.004), (0.011, wy, wz) if ang % 2 == 0 else (0.011, wy, wz), 'barrel')
    A.update(hg_x1=x + Lh, hg_w=r + 0.006, hg_zmid=0.0, hg_covers_gas=False)
def hg_slim(P, S, A):
    H = P['handguard']; x = A['hg_x0']; Lh = g(S, 'length', 0.24)
    pts = [(-0.021, 0.024), (0.021, 0.024), (0.030, 0.002), (0.024, -0.026), (-0.024, -0.026), (-0.030, 0.002)]
    H.prism(pts, Lh, g(S, 'material', 'furniture'), 0.003, plane='yz', c=x)
    for i in range(int(Lh / 0.045) - 1):
        for s in (-1, 1): H.box((x + 0.04 + i * 0.045, s * 0.0292, 0.002), (0.022, 0.002, 0.012), 'dark')
    A.update(hg_x1=x + Lh, hg_w=0.03, hg_zmid=0.002, hg_covers_gas=False)
def hg_shroud(P, S, A):
    H = P['handguard']; x = A['hg_x0']; Lh = g(S, 'length', 0.20); r = 0.024
    H.cyl((x + Lh / 2, 0, 0), r, Lh, 'body', seg=16)
    for i in range(int(Lh / 0.022)): H.cyl((x + 0.012 + i * 0.022, 0, 0), r + 0.0025, 0.006, 'barrel', seg=16)
    A.update(hg_x1=x + Lh, hg_w=r + 0.003, hg_zmid=0.0, hg_covers_gas=False)
def hg_none(P, S, A): A.update(hg_x1=A['x1'], hg_w=0.02, hg_zmid=0.0, hg_covers_gas=False)
HAND = {'wood_ak': hg_wood, 'rail_quad': hg_quad, 'slim_poly': hg_slim, 'ribbed_shroud': hg_shroud, 'none': hg_none}

# ---------------- BARREL + MUZZLE + GAS ----------------
def barrel(P, S, A, gas):
    B = P['barrel']; Lb = g(S, 'length', 0.42); r = g(S, 'radius', 0.0115); prof = g(S, 'profile', 'plain'); bx = A['x1'] - 0.01; mx = A['x1'] + Lb
    xc = (bx + mx) / 2; ln = mx - bx
    if prof == 'tapered': B.cyl((xc, 0, 0), r * 1.6, ln, 'barrel', r2=r, seg=16)
    elif prof == 'heavy': B.cyl((xc, 0, 0), r * 1.4, ln, 'barrel', seg=16)
    elif prof == 'shrouded':
        B.cyl((xc, 0, 0), r, ln, 'barrel', seg=16); B.cyl((bx + ln * 0.33, 0, 0), r * 2.3, ln * 0.66, 'body', seg=16, bevel=0.003)
    else: B.cyl((xc, 0, 0), r, ln, 'barrel', seg=16)
    mz = g(S, 'muzzle', 'brake'); A['muzzle_x'] = mx
    if mz == 'brake':
        B.cyl((mx + 0.025, 0, 0), r * 1.3, 0.05, 'barrel', seg=16, bevel=0.002)
        for dx in (0.015, 0.03): B.cyl((mx + dx, 0, 0), r * 1.32, 0.004, 'dark', seg=16)
    elif mz == 'flash_hider':
        B.cyl((mx + 0.03, 0, 0), r * 1.35, 0.06, 'barrel', r2=r * 1.1, seg=12)

# pk_rifle.py -- PARAMETRIC RIFLE TEMPLATE. build(spec_dict) -> (list of bpy objects, info). The AI step only emits `spec`.
import math, bpy
from pk_geo import Part, make_materials
from pk_parts import RECV, GRIP, MAG, STOCK, HAND, barrel, sights, trigger_guard, g

PART_NAMES = ['receiver', 'grip', 'magazine', 'stock', 'handguard', 'barrel', 'sights', 'trim']
def pick(table, S, key, default):
    st = (S or {}).get('style', default)
    if st not in table: raise ValueError(f'{key}.style={st!r} not in {sorted(table)}')
    return table[st]

def accents(P, A, lst, glow='glow'):
    T = P['trim']; w = A['w']
    for a in lst or []:
        if a == 'receiver_side':
            for s in (-1, 1): T.box(((A['x0'] + A['x1']) / 2 + 0.02, s * (w / 2 + 0.0008), A['zmid'] + 0.012), ((A['x1'] - A['x0']) * 0.5, 0.0016, 0.006), glow)
        elif a == 'receiver_top':
            T.box(((A['x0'] + A['x1']) / 2, 0, A['z_top'] + 0.0006), ((A['x1'] - A['x0']) * 0.6, 0.006, 0.0016), glow)
        elif a == 'handguard_side':
            for s in (-1, 1): T.box(((A['hg_x0'] + A['hg_x1']) / 2 + 0.01, s * (A['hg_w'] + 0.0006), A['hg_zmid'] + 0.002), (A['hg_x1'] - A['hg_x0'] - 0.06, 0.0016, 0.006), glow)
        elif a == 'magazine_window' and 'mag_mid' in A:
            x, z, rot, mw = A['mag_mid']
            for s in (-1, 1): T.box((x, s * (mw / 2 + 0.0006), z), (0.008, 0.0016, 0.07), glow, rot=(0, rot, 0))
        elif a == 'stock_side' and A.get('stock_len', 0) > 0:
            for s in (-1, 1): T.box((-A['stock_len'] * 0.5, s * 0.0215, 0.0), (A['stock_len'] * 0.5, 0.0016, 0.006), glow)
        elif a == 'barrel_ring':
            T.cyl((A['muzzle_x'] - 0.03, 0, 0), g(A.get('_b'), 'radius', 0.0115) * 1.5, 0.006, glow, seg=16)
        else: raise ValueError(f'accent {a!r} unknown/unavailable')

def build(spec):
    P = {n: Part(n) for n in PART_NAMES}; A = {}
    pick(RECV, spec.get('receiver'), 'receiver', 'ak_stamped')(P, spec.get('receiver', {}), A)
    GS = spec.get('grip', {}); pick(GRIP, GS, 'grip', 'ak_slanted')(P, GS, A)
    if GS.get('style') != 'none' and spec.get('trigger_guard', True): trigger_guard(P, GS, A)
    MS = spec.get('magazine', {}); pick(MAG, MS, 'magazine', 'curved')(P, MS, A)
    SS = spec.get('stock', {}); pick(STOCK, SS, 'stock', 'fixed_wood')(P, SS, A)
    HS = spec.get('handguard', {}); pick(HAND, HS, 'handguard', 'wood_ak')(P, HS, A)
    BS = spec.get('barrel', {}); A['_b'] = BS
    if 'hg_x0' in HS: pass
    barrel(P, BS, A, bool(spec.get('gas_tube', False)))
    sights(P, spec.get('sights', {}), A, g(BS, 'radius', 0.0115))
    accents(P, A, spec.get('accents'))
    mats = make_materials(spec.get('palette'))
    objs = [P[n].to_object(mats) for n in PART_NAMES if len(P[n].bm.faces)]

        if not len(P[n].bm.faces) and P[n].bm.is_valid: P[n].bm.free()
    return objs, A

|---|---|---|---|

| Tris | 1,452 | 948 | 1,412 |
| Non-manifold edges (per object) | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| UV on all objects | yes (7/7) | yes (8/8) | yes (7/7) |
| glTF validator | 0 errors, 0 warnings | 0/0 | 0/0 |

PoC 1 AK for comparison: 6.5/10, 4 rounds, ~15-20k tokens, 2,732 tris.

Adjustments made after looking: AK r1 to r2 fixed a near-black receiver that hid detail (palette) and tapered the barrel. Bullpup r1 to r2 fixed a plain white slab (palette), added more glow strips. SMG r1 to r2 fixed monochrome low contrast. All three fixes were palette or minor parameters. None changed the silhouette.

Mesh caveat (VERIFIED): "manifold" is per closed shell. Primitives overlap and are not unioned (bullpup receiver has 18 shells, AK barrel 6), same as PoC 1. All three are under 10k tris (6-15% of budget), so there is room for more detail.

## What the template could NOT express
Contoured bullpup stock/cheek weld (stock is a slab plus pad); sight position and optic/rail layout (fixed anchors, red dot reads as a block); organic grips and ergonomics; folded-stock state was not tested; wear, damage, normal maps and textures (flat colours only); any non-rifle class (pistol, shotgun, bolt-action, belt-fed, launcher); underbarrel, bipod, light, scope; per-part offsets; asymmetric left/right features.

## Cost and break-even
| | Tokens | Time |
|---|---|---|
| One-time template + kit build (counter, 68.7k total incl. ~6k reading PoC 1; ~60k net) | ~60-65k | ~10 min agent wall (16:39 to 16:48, 3 sandbox runs for bug fixes); a human would need roughly 4-6 h (UNVERIFIED) |
| From scratch per rifle (PoC 1, fixed prelude) | 15-20k | 4 rounds |
| Template per rifle, measured | 5-8k | 2 rounds |
| Saving per prompt | ~10-14k measured, ~12-16k on lean est. | |

Break-even is about **5-6 prompts** if every prompt fits the template (60k / ~11k), about 4 on the lean estimate, and about **10-12 prompts at a 50% fit rate** (misfits fall back to the next rung). Each new object class (pistol, vehicle, crate) needs its own template; I would guess 30-40k for the second (geo layer reused, UNVERIFIED).

## Verdict on the hypothesis
- Token cut: **2.5-3x measured, about 5x on the lean estimate**. The 5-10x target is not reached or proven. One-round success would approach 8-10x (about 2k) but this PoC never got a one-round pass: first JSONs were all palette-weak.
- Quality: equal or slightly better (7 / 6.5 / 7 vs 6.5), more consistent scale, UVs and part names by construction.
- Risk removed: the model emits data only, no executable code, so the static-rejection problem from PoC 1 largely disappears for this rung (UNVERIFIED in a real worker).
- Next: a vision step that picks palette automatically (the only fix needed every time); let the parts kit take part offsets in JSON; measure template-fit rate over 20+ real prompts; try parts-kit assembly rung (model writes a list of part calls) for misfits.
